chunks: Then as he was about to lay hands on the one who was their common enemy, he cried out: "O Moses, do you want to kill me as you killed that person yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant in the land and no peacemaker."

key_terms.يَبْطِشَ: to lay hands on / to seize

ai.seo_question: What did the Egyptian say to Moses when he was about to kill him?
ai.summary: In this verse from Surah Hud, the Egyptian reminds Moses of his previous act of killing a Copt, accusing him of becoming a tyrant in the land rather than a peacemaker. This moment highlights the transition of Moses from a solitary avenger to a leader facing the consequences of his actions, a key theme in Shia exegesis regarding the purification of the prophets. The accusation underscores the tension between Moses' divine mission and the human perception of his growing authority.
